key_insight: A physics-constrained, multi-fidelity turbulence model can be trained at affordable low Reynolds number and extrapolated to higher Reynolds numbers with formal cost scaling of O(log(Re)) under stated assumptions.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a path toward more accurate and computationally feasible turbulence predictions for wall-bounded engineering flows without paying the full cost of high-Re high-fidelity simulation.
method: Augment the Spalart–Allmaras RANS model with field inversion and machine learning.
Constrain the learned correction to preserve the law of the wall.
Train at low Re and deploy to higher Re with a mean-flow-aligned grid and fixed spanwise resolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful transfer from plane channel flow at Re_tau=1000 to Re_tau=5200, and from periodic hill training at Re_b=5600 to tests at Re_b=10595, 19000, and 37000, with lowest RMS error and nearly Re-independent error.
watch_item: The O(log(Re)) cost claim depends on specific grid, solver, and alignment assumptions, so practical scalability may differ outside those conditions.
paper_title: A formal log(Re)-cost framework for the engineering turbulence problem
